1.explanation:
• ComposedModal/ComposedModal.mdx: shows how the modal is composed and contains the transactional example with an input field.  
• Modal/Modal.mdx: describes base modal structure, padding rules, and content container sizing.  
• TextInput/TextInput.mdx: demonstrates how TextInput should behave and handle width (100% by default).  
• Form/Form.mdx + FormGroup/FormGroup.mdx + FormLabel/FormLabel.mdx: these docs outline the form layout pattern used inside the modal (wrappers around inputs) and any default spacing or width constraints applied by form primitives.  

Together, these documents cover the modal container’s layout and the form/input primitives that determine how the TextInput should stretch to fill its parent container, which is key to reproducing and fixing the regression in input width within the modal.
1.bug_scenario: In the current Storybook example for our ComposedModal (a transactional modal), the TextInput field that lives inside the modal’s form is not expanding to fill the full width of the modal content area. Instead there’s an unexpected right‐hand gap — the input stops short of the modal’s padding edge. In the “should be” artboard we can see that the input should stretch to the full width available (minus standard 16px/1rem horizontal padding). The elements involved are the ComposedModal wrapper (modal content container), any Form/FormGroup wrappers around the input, and the TextInput component itself.
